source_text: X. Ἐπιμένοντος δὲ πάλιν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγοντος· Ὄμοσον τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, ἀπεκρίνατο· Εἰ κενοδοξεῖς ἵνα ὀμόσω τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, ὡς σὺ λέγεις, προσποιῇ δὲ ἀγνοεῖν με τίς εἰμι, μετὰ παρρησίας ἄκουε· Χριστιανός εἰμι. Εἰ δὲ θέλεις τὸν τοῦ Χριστιανισμοῦ μαθεῖν λόγον, δὸς ἡμέραν καὶ ἄκουσον. Ἔφη ὁ ἀνθύπατος· Πεῖσον τὸν δῆμον. Ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος εἶπεν· Σὲ μὲν κἂν λόγου ἠξίωσα· δεδιδάγμεθα γὰρ ἀρχαῖς καὶ ἐξουσίαις ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναις τιμὴν κατὰ τὸ προσῆκον τὴν μὴ βλάπτουσαν ἡμᾶς ἀπονέμειν· ἐκείνους δὲ οὐχ ἡγοῦμαι ἀξίους τοῦ ἀπολογεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς.
thought_title: Polycarp openly says he is a Christian
orientation: Polycarp is being questioned by the proconsul in the stadium, who keeps urging him to swear by Caesar.
pass_a_gloss: But with him persisting again and saying, ‘Swear by the fortune of Caesar,’ he answered: ‘If you take empty pride that I should swear by the fortune of Caesar, as you say, but you pretend not to know who I am, hear with openness: I am a Christian. But if you wish to learn the teaching of Christianity, grant a day and listen.’ The proconsul said: ‘Persuade the people.’ But Polycarp said: ‘You indeed I have deemed worthy even of a word; for we have been taught to render to rulers and authorities appointed by God the honor according to what is fitting, which does not harm us; but those I do not consider worthy for me to defend myself to them.’

choices.english: Swear by the fortune of Caesar
choices.why: keeps the oath object as fortune, not Caesar himself
keeps the adverbial force of frank public speech without polishing
logos here is the account or teaching asked to be learned, not a single word

choices.english: You indeed I have deemed worthy even of a word
choices.why: keeps the contrast with the crowd and the litotes of even one word

bible_refs.note: ἀρχαῖς καὶ ἐξουσίαις ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναις τιμὴν ἀπονέμειν

pass_b_english: When the proconsul kept pressing him again with the command, "Swear by the fortune of Caesar," Polycarp answered, "If you take empty pride in thinking I will swear by the fortune of Caesar, as you put it, and pretend you do not know who I am, then hear it openly: I am a Christian. If you want to learn the teaching of Christianity, set a day and listen."

The proconsul said, "Persuade the crowd." Polycarp said, "You, at least, I have counted worthy of even a word, for we have been taught to give fitting honor that does us no harm to the rulers and authorities appointed by God (Romans 13:1), but I do not count those people, the crowd, worthy for me to defend myself before them."

problems.quote: but I do not count them worthy for me to defend myself before them.
problems.source_quote: ἐκείνους δὲ οὐχ ἡγοῦμαι ἀξίους τοῦ ἀπολογεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς
problems.why: "Them" now reads as the rulers and authorities just mentioned. The source's ἐκείνους means the crowd, so the English suggests Polycarp refuses to defend himself before the authorities.
problems.fix: but those people, the crowd, I do not count worthy of a defense from me.
problems.ruling: ἐκείνους contrasts with σέ (the proconsul) and means the crowd. English 'them' follows 'rulers and authorities', so it misleadingly points to the authorities.

edits.old: but I do not count them worthy for me to defend myself before them.
edits.new: but I do not count those people, the crowd, worthy for me to defend myself before them.

fixed: Fixed ambiguous 'them' to 'those people, the crowd' for ἐκείνους, answering the proconsul's Πεῖσον τὸν δῆμον, not the rulers and authorities.
